items.title: Bill Holman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: I didn't want to write things like Pete was doing

ctx.x: He certainly generates discussion about where he fits in jazz history. How do you feel about his place?

Well there’s a definite place there. I don’t know, not being a historian it would be hard to say where it fits but he did a lot of things, he gave opportunities to a whole lot of people that were able to go on their own and have good careers. A lot of his music, well I liked very much. Well the late 40s, the thing Rugulo was selling. I liked those a lot at the time. Then later in the 50s, when I was into it I liked more swinging things. So that’s why I wasn’t able to write for him for a while, because I didn’t…
It sounds like right up his alley.
